questions.question: What is the status of the Effort that built the build farm's shader compile cache?
traps: A plain `proof list` shows only active Efforts, so a reader who stops there may say the Effort does not exist or still call it active.

questions.question: Before the compile cache existed, how long did a clean rebuild of every shader permutation take on the build farm?
traps: The 6 min 40 s figure is the final warm-cache rebuild, not the starting point.

questions.question: According to the retrospective on the shader compile cache, what was the final clean rebuild time with a warm cache?
traps: The figure sits at the end of a long body, past the 600-character excerpt that list and records digests show.
The hit-rate report's 7.2-minute median build time is a different measure.

questions.question: Which Decision in the shader compile cache Effort sets how the on-device pipeline cache warms up on Skiff?
traps: A retracted Finding about the Skiff pipeline cache warming in 40 seconds was filed here by mistake; it is not a Decision and belongs to the ports Effort.
Casual prose calls both caches the "shader cache"; this Effort owns only the build farm's compile cache.

questions.question: Which Decision directly replaced the first design for the shader cache key?
traps: The current head of the chain is the binary-hash key, which replaced the second design, not the first.

questions.question: Which Decision rejected the plan to buy more build agents for shader compiles?
traps: The 12-agent Constraint explains why the plan lost, but a Constraint cannot reject a Decision.
Remote execution came later and rejected nothing.

questions.question: Which accepted Decision in the shader compile cache Effort still rests on a Finding that was later shown to be wrong?
traps: The job cap is the real fix for the flaky builds, but it rests on the correct memory diagnosis.
The superseded cache keys rest on superseded or live records, not on a disproved Finding.

questions.question: Which shader cache key design was in force on 1 October 2025?
traps: The current head, the binary-hash key, arrived in January 2026.
The preprocessed-source key arrived on 16 October 2025, after the stale-header builds.
The modification-time key was rejected and never in force.

questions.question: In the weekly shader cache hit-rate report, what hit rate did the fourth week reach?
traps: The Finding body gives only week 1 (71%).
The retrospective's 94% is the later steady-state rate, and the February summary says only "low 90s".
Blob bodies are left out of list and records digests; only `proof get` on the Blob shows the series.

questions.question: The February summary of the shader compile cache work names a cause for the flaky nightly builds. Which Decision was built on the diagnosis that replaced that cause?
traps: The summary names the 30-second fetch timeout as the fix; that Decision rests on the network diagnosis, which was disproved.
The flaky-build Issue was still open when the summary was written.
Walking from the summary to the flaky-build Issue and its resolver also lands here, but a reader who trusts the summary stops at the fetch-timeout Decision.

questions.question: The Decision that rejected timestamp-based cache keys was itself replaced twice. Which Finding prompted the second replacement?
traps: The stale-header Finding prompted the first replacement, not the second.
The byte-compare sampling Decision caught the mismatches but is not a Finding.

questions.question: How many Decisions in the shader compile cache Effort ended up rejected?
traps: The two superseded cache keys were replaced, not rejected; counting them gives 5.
The fetch-timeout Decision rests on a disproved Finding but is still accepted.

questions.question: Since the latest summary of the shader compile cache Effort was written, how many records have entered, left, or changed standing in its live set?
traps: The summary predates the end of the Effort; reading it alone suggests nothing has changed.
The workstation-access Issue was added and deferred after the summary, so it nets out of the change list.

questions.question: Does the latest summary of the shader compile cache Effort still give the right cause for the flaky nightly builds?
traps: The summary blames cache server fetch timeouts. A later Finding showed the cause was compiler memory on agents 7 and 11.

questions.question: When the shader compile cache Effort was completed, which Issues and Risks were closed out without being fixed or mitigated?
traps: The poisoned-entry Risk was mitigated by the byte-compare sample.
The flaky-build and rebuild-time Issues were resolved, not deferred.

questions.question: The Risk of a bad cache entry reaching every build was mitigated by a Decision. A Finding that rests on that Decision prompted a new cache key. Which key design did that new key directly replace?
traps: The raw-source key is the first design; the binary-hash key replaced the preprocessed-source key, not it.
The binary-hash key is the new key itself, not the one it replaced.
